replacementLevel.basis: measured from 656 skaters on league-minimum standard contracts — at or under 1.1% of the cap, signed at age 25 or older
replacementLevel.why: Replacement is what a club can sign for the minimum, not a percentile of a distribution. Entry-level deals are excluded — a cheap contract only measures replacement when the player was free to sign anywhere and nobody bid more.

marketRate.why: What clubs pay for a goal above replacement, from regressing cap share on production across every one-way standard signing. Corroborated by walking the pay ladder end to end, which needs no linear assumption and lands within 10%.

budgetConstraintRejected.whyRejected: It assumes a club's whole discretionary payroll buys the production this metric measures. It does not — goaltending, defence beyond on-ice expected goals, special teams and inefficiency all consume cap — so dividing all of the money by some of the value inflates the rate about sixfold. At this rate a median full-season skater would cost $6.9M and the best season on record $67.5M against a $20.8M legal maximum.

agreement.verdict: the two routes disagree by design; the budget route is rejected above
